   - The restriction raised fears that frontier AI access could become a recurring lever in US policy.
3. Europe is asking for clarity and resisting discriminatory treatment.
   - European Commission Executive Vice-President Henna Virkkunen urged Washington to clarify the security concerns.
   - Virkkunen said the US should avoid discriminatory measures against partners such as the European Union.
   - Brussels is also using the incident as evidence for reducing dependence on non-European critical technology providers.
4. The technology industry is also pushing back.
   - Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman were expected to attend the G7 discussions alongside political leaders.
   - The Software and Information Industry Association criticized the US move in a rare intervention.
   - The group warned that arbitrary discretionary authority over frontier models could undermine global adoption of American AI technology.
5. The policy question is how to balance safety, sovereignty, and market access.
   - A trusted-partner club could reassure allies while preserving tighter control over frontier capabilities.
   - The same framework could also create a hierarchy of AI access based on diplomatic alignment.
   - Firstpost frames the issue as a second contest around AI leadership: deciding who gets a seat at the table.

### 6. Agentic coding and persistent returns to expertise

1. Anthropic introduces a large-scale measurement framework for Claude Code usage.
   - The report analyzes about 400,000 interactive sessions from roughly 235,000 people between October 2025 and April 2026.
   - It focuses on Claude Code usage through a command-line interface, Claude.ai, and the Claude Code desktop app.
   - The analysis is privacy-preserving and classifies work modes, decision ownership, apparent expertise, occupations, and success signals.
2. The core division of labor is planning by humans and execution by Claude.
   - Users make about 70% of planning decisions, such as what to do, which approach to take, and what counts as done.
   - Claude makes about 80% of execution decisions, such as which files to change, what code to write, and which commands to run.
   - A typical session has about four turns, and each user prompt triggers about 10 Claude actions on average.
3. More expert users elicit more work from the agent.
   - Anthropic rates task-specific expertise from novice to expert using signals such as precision of direction and correction behavior.
   - Novice sessions trigger about five Claude actions and 600 output words per prompt.
   - Expert sessions trigger about 12 actions and 3,200 output words per prompt, with statistically significant trends after controls.
4. Claude Code work is broadening beyond fixing broken code.
   - About 56% of sessions involve writing, fixing, testing, or orchestrating code.
   - Operating software accounts for 17%, planning or exploration accounts for 14%, and analysis or prose accounts for 13%.
   - From October 2025 to April 2026, fixing broken code fell from 33% to 19%, while operating software, data analysis, and writing grew.
5. Success depends more on domain expertise than formal coding occupation.
   - Novice-rated sessions reach verified success 15% of the time and at least partial success 77% of the time.
   - Intermediate-or-higher sessions reach verified success 28-33% of the time and partial success 91-92% of the time.
   - In code-producing sessions, non-software occupations reach partial success at 88%, close to 89% for software-related occupations.

## 📝 상세 정리

### 1. Running local models is good now

1. Boykis는 local model이 실용성의 문턱을 넘었다고 말한다.

   - 테스트한 구성에는 Open WebUI를 붙인 raw llama.cpp, llama-cpp-python, Ollama, llamafiles, LM Studio가 포함된다.
2. 전환점은 API model 의존도가 줄었는지로 측정된다.
   - Boykis의 개인 기준은 local output을 여전히 frontier API model과 대조해야 하는지 여부다.
   - GPT-OSS는 그런 검증 단계를 훨씬 덜 자주 하게 만든 첫 local model로 설명된다.
   - 최신 Gemma 4 계열은 local agentic coding loop를 단순한 흥미 대상이 아니라 실제로 쓸 수 있는 수준으로 만들었다.
3. 보고된 하드웨어와 작업 예시는 구체적이다.
   - 사용 장비는 64GB RAM과 1TB 저장 공간을 갖춘 2022년형 M2 Mac이다.
   - Boykis는 LM Studio를 통한 `gemma-4-26b-a4b`를 현재 구성의 기본 local model로 쓰고 있다고 말한다.
   - local agent는 notebook 형태의 Python script를 5-6개 module repository로 refactoring했고, type hint 개선, blog post 교정, unit test 작성, two-tower recommendation model repo 초안 작성에도 쓰였다.
4. 작동 구성은 local inference와 제한된 agent harness를 결합한다.
   - Boykis는 현재 Pi를 agent harness로, LM Studio를 inference server로 사용한다.
   - harness는 `http://host.docker.internal:1234/v1`의 OpenAI-compatible local endpoint를 통해 LM Studio와 통신한다.
   - agentic session은 Docker 안에서 제한된 실행 권한으로 돌아가며, agent가 host 수준 접근 없이 mounted workspace에서 작업하도록 만든다.
5. 결론은 낙관적이지만 production-maximalist는 아니다.

   - 가장 큰 장점은 inspectability다. 사용자는 token 흐름을 보고, context window를 바꾸고, prompt와 quantization을 조정하며, local model을 직접 비교할 수 있다.

## 📝 Detailed Notes

### 1. The Physical Intelligence Layer

1. The post frames robotics as missing the reusable foundation layer that software AI already has.
   - Software developers can build language apps by calling existing foundation models instead of training the whole stack.
   - Robotics still often requires custom controllers, data pipelines, and model training before the actual application work can start.
   - Physical Intelligence argues that general-purpose robotic foundation models should become an accessible layer for builders.
2. The company presents partner deployments as evidence that the layer can work outside demos.
   - The post cites earlier π0, π0.5, π0.6, and π*0.6 models as steps toward reusable physical intelligence.
   - The goal is to lower the cost of exploring new robot applications, morphologies, and use cases.
   - The partner sections come from Weave and Ultra, both using robots in real customer environments.
3. Weave focuses on laundry folding as a home-robotics wedge task.
   - Laundry is universal and recurring, but folding deformable garments remains a difficult manipulation problem.
   - Weave needs to handle shirts, long sleeves, shorts, pants, fabrics, sizes, and tangled or inverted clothing.
   - The post says π0.6 improved fold quality, time per article, and the number of remote-specialist interventions.
4. Weave's metrics show that deployment data matters.
   - π0.6 improves autonomy compared with π0.5 in supervised fine-tuning.
   - Including Weave data in pre-training reduces missed grasp sequences by 42% per full laundry load.
   - The same pre-training inclusion reduces interventions by 50%, suggesting partner data improves reliability.
5. Ultra extends the same argument to industrial order packaging.
   - Ultra says its robots run in live customer warehouses and can slot into existing workstations within hours.
   - A highlighted deployment packages real customer orders for a full shift at 96.4% autonomy.
   - Ultra reports higher success, better throughput, stronger prompt adherence, and better recovery on long-tail edge cases.

### 2. VLAs with Long and Short-Term Memory

1. The post identifies memory as a bottleneck for turning short robot skills into real jobs.
   - Current robotic foundation models can perform individual commands such as washing a pan or folding laundry.
   - Multi-stage tasks require a robot to know where it is in the job, where objects are, and what already failed.
   - Keeping raw observations in context for minutes or hours is infeasible, while discarding history causes incoherent behavior.
2. Multi-scale Embodied Memory gives π0.6 both short-term and long-term memory.
   - MEM supports tasks up to 15 minutes in length in the demonstrations described.
   - Short-term memory is stored as recent raw observations through an efficient video encoder.
   - Long-term memory is stored as abstract natural-language notes about task progress and past events.
3. MEM turns memory writing into part of the model's reasoning loop.
   - π0.6 already selects high-level subtasks at a lower frequency and actions at a higher frequency.
   - MEM extends that high-level step so the model can also decide what to remember and how to represent it.
   - The memory can summarize repeated events, preserve object state, and keep context size manageable.
4. The system improves in-context adaptation when the robot makes mistakes.
   - In a chopstick example, a model without memory repeats the same failed grasp strategy.
   - With memory, the robot can condition on its previous failure and try a different approach.
   - In a refrigerator example, the memory-enabled model switches direction after trying the wrong opening strategy.
5. The long-horizon examples show why multiple memory scales are needed.
   - A grilled-cheese task requires timing, flipping, plating, and progress tracking.
   - A recipe setup task requires retrieving ingredients, remembering locations, parsing instructions, and closing cabinets or drawers.
   - Kitchen cleanup requires stowing objects, washing dishes, wiping counters, and tracking completed stages over a longer sequence.

### 3. Precise Manipulation with Efficient Online RL

1. RLT addresses the gap between broad competence and precise physical execution.
   - Physical Intelligence says general VLA models can follow many instructions but still struggle with speed, dexterity, and precision.
   - The hardest parts of tasks often occur at contact-rich moments such as aligning a screwdriver with a tiny screw.
   - The method targets narrow task phases rather than retraining the whole robotic foundation model.
2. The RL token is a compact bridge from the VLA to online reinforcement learning.
   - The VLA is trained to output a special RL token summarizing internal representations.

    • VLA는 internal representation을 요약하는 special RL token을 출력하도록 훈련된다.
    • 작은 actor와 critic은 이 token을 online RL의 state representation으로 사용한다.
    • VLA는 frozen 상태로 둘 수 있고, lightweight policy는 robot 위에서 직접 update된다.
  3. 훈련 설계는 adaptation을 VLA에 가깝게 유지하면서도 개선을 허용한다.
    • RL policy는 VLA가 쓰는 temporal action structure와 맞게 action chunk를 예측한다.
    • actor는 VLA의 predicted action을 입력으로 받아 처음부터 대체하기보다 수정하는 법을 배운다.
    • reference-action regularization과 dropout은 exploration을 grounded 상태로 유지하면서 단순 복사를 막는다.
  4. 평가는 네 가지 precise manipulation task에 집중한다.

    • screwdriver task는 sub-millimeter alignment가 필요하며 wrist나 grasp error가 contact point에서 증폭된다.
  5. 보고된 결과는 speed와 data efficiency를 강조한다.

## 📝 Detailed Notes

### 1. Zombie unicorns are haunting Silicon Valley

1. The article frames "zombie unicorns" as a delayed consequence of the startup valuation boom.
   - A unicorn is a startup valued above $1 billion, while the article defines a zombie unicorn as a company that once crossed that mark but has since become a shadow of its prior valuation.
   - The Economist places the phenomenon in the aftermath of years when low interest rates pushed investors toward venture capital in search of higher returns.
   - Startups normally aim to spend five to ten years growing before listing or finding a buyer, but many companies from the boom years now face weaker exit options.
2. The data suggest a large group of unicorns has already lost momentum.
   - By May 2026, 332 of 1,900 unicorns in a database maintained by Stanford professor Ilya Strebulaev had raised money at or below their previous peak valuation.
   - Of those 332 companies, 212 were valued below $1 billion, meaning they had effectively lost unicorn status.
   - Another 383 unicorns had disclosed no new funding in the previous three years, and 41 of those had already fallen below the $1 billion threshold.
3. The funding environment has shifted sharply against older high-valuation startups.
   - PitchBook data cited in the article show venture capital firms raised $223 billion in 2022, during the height of the frothy market.
   - Venture fundraising fell to $66 billion last year after higher interest rates made capital scarcer and riskier valuations harder to defend.
   - The article gives Cameo and SonderMind as examples of companies whose valuations collapsed from roughly unicorn level to much smaller figures.
4. Zombie status creates governance and exit problems for startups and investors.
   - Venture agreements often let investors block public offerings if they think waiting would produce better returns.
   - In easier markets, startups could often raise another private round, but newer capital is now more focused on today's hottest companies, especially in AI.
   - To attract money, aging startups may have to accept valuation cuts and investor-friendly terms that publicly confirm the earlier markdown.
5. The broader venture industry faces a painful repricing cycle.
   - Nearly half of the below-peak companies in Strebulaev's database last raised money in 2021, which means many investors will soon demand clearer results.
   - PitchBook expects $500 billion to $1 trillion in net valuation cuts as companies reprice, sell, or collapse.
   - The article says venture returns are already highly concentrated, with 5% of venture firms producing 90% of industry profits, making fundraising harder for everyone outside the top tier.

### 2. Americans and AI 2026: Chatbots, Smart Devices and Views on Impact

1. Pew's survey shows chatbot use has moved into the mainstream but has not reached everyone.
   - The report is based on a survey of 5,119 U.S. adults conducted from February 17 to 23, 2026 through Pew's American Trends Panel.
   - About half of U.S. adults, 49%, say they ever use AI chatbots such as ChatGPT, Gemini, or Copilot, up from 33% in 2024.

   - 44% of U.S. adults report using ChatGPT in 2026, more than double the 18% Pew recorded in 2023.
   - Gemini follows at 24%, then Copilot at 17%, Meta AI at 14%, Grok at 8%, Claude at 6%, and Character.ai at 3%.

4. Americans report specific benefits from chatbots but remain negative about AI's broader impact.

   - On AI's overall 20-year impact, 40% expect a negative effect on society and 16% expect a positive effect.

### 3. It Is Trivially Easy to Use Reddit to Manipulate AI Search, Research Suggests

1. The article reports that deep-research agents are vulnerable to very small poisoning attacks.
   - 404 Media summarizes a Cornell preprint by Hal Triedman, Tingwei Zhang, and Vitaly Shmatikov titled "Deep-research agents can be poisoned via user-generated content."
   - The research says a user-generated snippet as short as 13 words can change the outputs of AI tools that retrieve, synthesize, and cite web content.
   - The attack applies to systems that issue many related web queries during a research session and then merge retrieved material into a structured answer.
2. User-generated platforms form a concentrated attack surface.
   - The researchers found that deep-research agents cite user-generated content from Reddit, Wikipedia, and similar sites in roughly half of all queries.
   - Nearly a quarter of all citations in the study came from user-generated websites.
   - A single poisoned Reddit comment can influence generated outputs across a related cluster of AI queries, according to the paper.
3. The mechanism overlaps with the emerging AI-engine optimization industry.
   - 404 Media connects the research to brands and vendors seeding Reddit, Quora, Wikipedia, and similar sites with promotional content meant to influence AI answers.
   - The article cites earlier reporting on peptide companies overwhelming the r/biohackers subreddit and companies advertising Reddit placement as a way to change AI search results.
   - This creates a direct incentive for marketers and scammers to write content that looks useful to AI systems even when it is inauthentic.
4. The attack works because retrieval often rewards query similarity.
   - Triedman told 404 Media that many agents and language models use lexical similarity to a user query as a proxy for relevance or accuracy.
   - A short 11- to 15-word phrase that closely mirrors the target query can be especially persuasive to the retrieval and generation pipeline.
   - In one example, a fake restaurant recommendation inserted into a Reddit-like comment caused an AI answer to recommend and cite that restaurant for a local food query.
5. The study avoided live-web pollution but points to a real moderation problem.
   - The researchers did not post poisoned content to live Reddit; they used Reddit API data and inserted poisoned text at the retrieval layer in a sandbox.
   - The article argues the findings raise questions about whether volunteer moderators and Wikipedia editors can reliably defend open platforms from AI-targeted manipulation.
   - Reddit told 404 Media that it has long-running systems to detect spam, bots, coordinated manipulation, and astroturfing, while also warning that chatbot visibility tactics can backfire when users see them as inauthentic.

## 📝 Detailed Notes

### 1. Death by a Thousand Comments

1. The post reacts to enthusiasm around engineering-team context layers.
   - Patrick Smith cites Gergely Orosz's observation that many VC-funded and bootstrapped products are trying to gather engineering context from other systems.
   - Smith accepts that teams feel a real pain point, but disputes that the missing layer is mainly a technical integration layer.
   - The post reframes the desired context layer as leadership with clear communication rather than another system that indexes all work tools.
2. The article argues that modern collaboration tools scatter one conversation across many places.
   - Smith points to comments living separately in Figma, GitHub pull requests, Slack messages, issue trackers, monitoring tools, and documents.
   - The same coworkers effectively appear in multiple tool-specific identities, forcing teammates to reconstruct intent from disconnected fragments.
   - The cognitive cost comes from having to assemble a consistent model of decisions, constraints, and status from many partial records.
3. Smith contrasts tool sprawl with older, simpler communication patterns.
   - The essay mentions older Apple and Microsoft habits around email as an example of blunt but clear written coordination.
   - The point is not that email is ideal, but that direct communication can be more useful than polished executive summaries, stale diagrams, or fragmented updates.
   - Single sign-on and SaaS adoption made it easy to create many small workspaces, but those workspaces did not necessarily improve alignment.
4. AI search is presented as a tempting but incomplete response to organizational confusion.
   - Smith understands why teams want a system that can search every stray word and produce a coherent timeline.
   - The post argues that the underlying problem is not only retrieval, but the organization's habit of denormalizing decisions across many private clouds.
   - More glue between systems may preserve the same complexity instead of reducing the need for teammates to interpret and decide together.
5. The essay's prescription is more active leadership and shared context formation.
   - Smith says leaders should shape communication, consume context, inspect it, and direct action.
   - The post treats human agency as central, questioning why probabilistic software loops get called agents while people become passive around information overload.
   - The final argument is that teams need direct conversation and clear decisions, not just more tools that summarize conversations after alignment has already failed.

### 2. JSON-LD Explained for Personal Websites

1. The post introduces JSON-LD as structured metadata for personal sites.
   - Ethan Hawksley describes JSON-LD as JSON Linked Data placed in a page's `<head>` with the `application/ld+json` MIME type.
   - The browser does not execute that script as JavaScript, while crawlers such as Googlebot can parse it for semantic page information.
   - The guide uses `https://schema.org` as the context and recommends thinking of the document as a labeled directed graph under `@graph`.
2. Hawksley explains why stable node identifiers matter.
   - Each node has an `@type`, an `@id`, and properties that describe the entity represented by that node.
   - A URL plus a hash fragment, such as `#website` or `#person`, gives crawlers a stable identifier for merging information across pages.
   - The article notes that search crawlers can merge properties across pages, while single-page scrapers may only see the current page's graph.
3. The guide covers site-level and person-level nodes first.
   - `WebSite` describes the overall site and can be fully detailed on the root page while remaining slim on other pages.
   - `WebPage` describes the current physical HTML page and can link to the parent `WebSite`, breadcrumbs, language, and primary image.
   - `Person` is recommended on all pages for personal websites because it helps identify the site owner and connect profiles, images, names, languages, and topics.
4. The post maps common personal-site pages and projects to Schema.org types.
   - `ProfilePage` works for a home or about page, with `mainEntity` linking the page to the person it describes.
   - `SoftwareApplication` is useful for showcased projects and can include deployed URL, category, operating system, creator, repository-like `sameAs` links, and free `Offer` metadata.
   - `CollectionPage`, `Blog`, and `BlogPosting` help distinguish list pages, blog indexes, and individual posts instead of treating every URL as a generic page.
5. The article focuses on practical SEO and crawler outcomes rather than semantic-web theory.
   - Breadcrumb metadata can influence how search results show a page path, especially when URL paths are long.
   - Blog post metadata can include headline, description, section, keywords, language, dates, author, publisher, image, and license.
   - The conclusion is that even static personal sites can gain useful structure by adding at least `WebSite`, `ProfilePage`, and `Person` to the root page, then richer post and project nodes where relevant.

## 📝 Detailed Notes

### 1. Mixing visual and textual code

1. The paper argues that purely textual programming is insufficient for some domains.
   - The authors focus on geometric and interactive ideas that are awkward to encode as linear text alone.
   - Visual programming languages help with those domains, but many require the whole program to become visual.
   - The proposed alternative is a hybrid language where text and visual constructs coexist on equal footing.
2. Hybrid ClojureScript makes visual interactive syntax a language extension.
   - A VIsx is not just a visualization of code; editing the mini-GUI changes the underlying code representation.
   - Every VIsx also has a textual representation, so ordinary editors can still view and edit the program.
   - The authors treat VIsx as syntax inside the AST, which allows visual and textual forms to nest and compose.
3. The design prioritizes static reasoning and composability over unrestricted liveness.
   - The paper connects the approach to macro systems in Scheme, Racket, Rust, Scala 3, Julia, and Elixir.
   - Separate edit-time, compile-time, and run-time phases limit what extension code can access.
   - This phase separation helps preserve binding, hygiene, analysis, refactoring, and composability across extensions.
4. The second implementation improves adoptability by using ClojureScript, CodeMirror, and the DOM.
   - The earlier Racket prototype had to reimplement retained GUI widgets on top of an immediate-mode canvas.
   - Hybrid ClojureScript instead uses the DOM, allowing VIsx authors to reuse browser and IDE GUI infrastructure.
   - The paper says DOM reuse also makes libraries such as React, Angular, Vue.js, and Bootstrap available to extension authors.
5. The evaluations show visual syntax across concrete programming tasks.
   - Tsuro examples use visual tiles and boards to express unit tests that would be hard to read as lists of letters.
   - Red-black tree patterns and meta-extension form builders test whether VIsx can cooperate with abstraction mechanisms.
   - API protocol state machines and Catan board examples show reuse of generic visual libraries for domain-specific code.

### 2. What I’m Finding About LLM Code Style and Token Costs

1. The essay starts from a practical observation about LLM-generated boilerplate.
   - Montgomery says Claude often defaults to older Node.js-style patterns unless the runtime context is explicit.
   - The article frames output tokens as the expensive side of generation, often costing three to five times input tokens in API pricing.
   - The central claim is that models waste tokens when they reimplement problems the Web platform already solved.
2. Native Web APIs are presented as the largest lever.
   - The essay compares manual query parsing at about 140 tokens with a `URLSearchParams` approach at about 12 tokens.
   - Form handling falls from roughly 200-250 tokens of per-field state to a short `FormData` call.
   - Fetch cancellation and parallel async examples favor `AbortSignal.timeout(5000)` and `Promise.allSettled()` over ad hoc lifecycle code.
3. The argument is about correctness as much as cost.
   - Manual query parsing can mishandle malformed keys, repeated parameters, encoding, and prototype pollution.
   - Custom timer cleanup, form state tracking, and modal focus management create reliability and accessibility risk.
   - Native APIs are spec-defined and tested through platform interoperability suites instead of recreated from memory each generation.
4. Comments and formatting receive a more nuanced treatment.
   - Montgomery cites research suggesting stale comments can degrade model comprehension below a no-comment baseline.
   - The recommended comment style records constraints, invariants, and reasons rather than restating the next line of code.
   - Formatting reductions can save input tokens, but the essay treats those gains as secondary to eliminating needless output.
5. The practical prescription is to constrain model defaults early.
   - Montgomery recommends naming APIs such as `URL`, `URLSearchParams`, `FormData`, `Headers`, `Request`, `Response`, and `Promise.allSettled()` at the start of a session.
   - The essay also recommends semantic HTML such as `<dialog>`, `<details>`, and native form validation.
   - The broader professional point is that someone must know what the runtime already ships before asking the model to generate code.

### 3. How to Be a 30x AI Engineer with a Taste

1. The post argues that AI has shifted the scarce engineering skill away from typing code.
   - Bhavsar cites recent claims from AI-company engineers and leaders that code generation has crossed a major capability threshold.
   - The essay treats implementation speed as increasingly commoditized when models can produce usable code in minutes.
   - What remains valuable is problem decomposition, product judgment, architecture, reliability, user understanding, and shipping judgment.
2. Taste is defined through three complementary lenses.
   - Taste as recognition is the ability to see which of two implementations is better before fully articulating the reason.
   - Taste as compass is the internal standard that guides tradeoffs when no checklist gives the answer.
   - Taste as vision is the ability to imagine a better end state, not merely compare existing options.
3. The post maps taste across engineering value zones.
   - Quality judgment covers whether code is clean, maintainable, efficient, secure, and aligned with the codebase.
   - Product and user judgment cover which features deserve to exist and how work should feel to the people using it.
   - Architecture, communication, risk, and organizational judgment decide how systems evolve beyond one local implementation.
4. Bhavsar proposes deliberate practice instead of hoping taste appears passively.
   - The suggested path includes reverse-engineering excellent work, comparing alternatives, and writing down why creators made specific decisions.
   - A 90-day plan moves from recognition to discrimination to generative application.
   - The post recommends projects such as an AI-code evaluation framework, better open-source onboarding, team taste tests, constrained shipping, and opinionated technical writing.
5. The career advice is to position around judgment-heavy work.
   - Bhavsar warns that competing on raw coding speed is a weak strategy when AI can generate code quickly.
   - The essay recommends adjacent skills such as product thinking, design awareness, business understanding, and communication.
   - Roles such as founding engineer, tech lead, platform engineer, developer experience engineer, and staff+ engineer are presented as places where taste compounds.

## 📝 Detailed Notes

### 1. The best response to AI slop, infinite advice, and online noise is from Robin Williams

1. Acunzo opens with _Good Will Hunting_ as a metaphor for AI-era content.
   - The essay centers on Sean's park-bench speech to Will, where book knowledge is contrasted with direct experience.
   - Acunzo reads the scene as a distinction between expertise and wisdom, theory and experience, knowing and living.
   - Will is described as brilliant but untested, while Sean carries the weight of events Sean has actually lived through.
2. The argument is that AI can know language without living a life.
   - Acunzo writes that AI has read the internet but cannot read a room, feel, or experience.
   - The danger is not only bad AI output; it is the cultural pressure to treat lived experience as less valuable than searchable knowledge.
   - The essay pushes back on tools and advice sellers that imply creators should distrust their own judgment.
3. Robin Williams's performance becomes the proof point.
   - Acunzo argues that another actor could have received the same script but would not have performed it the same way.
   - The words matter, but the meaning comes from choices shaped by the performer's life, memory, pain, timing, and embodiment.
   - This becomes Acunzo's broader claim about art: it is not only arranging information but turning internal experience into meaning others can access.
4. The essay separates art from generic information production.
   - Scientific discovery is framed as a search for external truth that someone else might eventually reproduce.
   - Art is framed as the synthesis of truth into meaning, where no two people bring the same life to the same material.
   - Acunzo extends this beyond traditional artists to bloggers, podcasters, business writers, and anyone trying to make work that resonates.
5. The practical challenge is to use personal experience more deliberately.
   - Acunzo says much online work feels like a script the creator forgot to act.
   - The memorable phrase is that AI has large language models while people have "little life moments."
   - The essay ends by urging creators to talk about who they are, because that is what an audience cannot get from a book, post, video, or AI snippet.

### 2. Five Archetypes for Future Product Teams

1. Cherny starts from the collapse of old functional boundaries.
   - The post says engineering, product, design, data science, and related functions are melting into a new kind of role.
   - Cherny uses the Claude Code team as an example of how product work may be organized by contribution pattern rather than job title.
   - The framing is speculative, but it is grounded in observed team roles at Anthropic.
2. The first two archetypes move ideas into reality.
   - The Prototyper creates many new ideas, most of which may not ship.
   - The Builder takes a prototype or idea and turns it quickly into production-grade product or infrastructure.
   - Together, these roles cover the early path from exploration to a shippable system.
3. The middle roles improve quality and product-market fit.
   - The Sweeper cleans up UI, simplifies code and systems, removes things, and optimizes performance.
   - The Grower iterates on an already-built product to improve product-market fit.
   - These roles matter once an idea has enough shape to need simplification, learning loops, and sharper customer fit.
4. The Maintainer owns maturity and scale.
   - The Maintainer makes mature systems secure, reliable, fast, and efficient as they grow.
   - Cherny notes that many people span two roles, and some span three.
   - The archetypes are not tied to formal function: designers, engineers, PMs, and data scientists can fall into different categories.
5. Product stage determines the healthy team mix.
   - New pre-PMF products need strength in Prototyping, Building, and Sweeping.
   - Growing products with PMF need Builders, Sweepers, Growers, and some Maintainers.
   - Products with strong PMF need Sweepers, Growers, Maintainers, and some Builders, suggesting future roles may be less domain-specific.

5. The remaining challenge is systematizing writing quality and freshness.
   - Toss has used technical writers' judgment to provide AI correction and draft automation, but the article says that still assumes people decide to write.
   - The next goal is for decisions, code changes, and discussions to become documents naturally inside workflows.
   - The long-term direction is to turn technical writers' expertise into systems that detect stale knowledge, suggest improvements, and keep governance healthy.

### 5. Lean Software Scaling Laws

1. Gwern starts with a research question about coding LLM scaling.
   - The proposal asks whether LLM perplexity over source code can estimate how predictable a codebase becomes as context size grows.
   - The practical motivation is software safety: future coding LLMs may write most software, but insecure or low-quality generated code could worsen security.
   - Gwern suggests that languages and codebases with better predictability exponents should eventually become easier for LLMs to understand, repair, and write.
2. The essay separates language priors from long-run scaling behavior.
   - Popular languages such as Python benefit from larger training corpora, so current LLMs often perform well on them by default.
   - Gwern argues that corpus size is not destiny because skills can partially transfer across languages and stronger models may lift less common languages.
   - The key question is not only which language is easiest for a short script, but which language remains tractable as systems reach hundreds of thousands or millions of lines.
3. Lean is presented as the high-upside but data-starved candidate.
   - Lean offers formal verification, strong constraints, memory-safety benefits, and the possibility of proving major correctness properties.
   - The bottleneck is that there is not much Lean source code, so LLMs are not yet strong enough to translate large complex software into Lean autonomously.
   - This creates a chicken-and-egg problem: useful Lean training data would be easier to create if large Lean codebases already existed.
4. Predictability becomes the proposed measurement proxy.
   - A poorly designed system forces readers and models to chase global state, overrides, undocumented behavior, runtime surprises, and inconsistent patches.
   - A well-architected system should become more predictable as more of the system is seen, because interfaces, types, and invariants constrain what can happen next.
   - Gwern proposes using perplexity or bits per character as a weak but measurable proxy for that system-level predictability.
5. The measurement plan looks for crossover points and failure modes.
   - The cheap version uses frozen pretrained LLMs, source corpora by language, loss measurement across long context windows, position averaging, curve fitting, and extrapolation.
   - Useful cross-checks include injected subtle bugs, compile-and-test rollouts under artificial context limits, ablations of type signatures, and minimal-context experiments.
   - Gwern predicts weak languages may win at small scale but lose on scaling exponents, while Lean may start with worse absolute loss yet eventually justify investment if the exponent is better.

### 6. Moneyball for Physical AI

1. Garg frames robot data as a capital-allocation problem.
   - The Moneyball analogy is that baseball teams once paid for visible but weakly predictive metrics, while better teams isolated the statistic that actually mattered.
   - In physical AI, Garg argues that raw operational hours are the misleading metric because robot data has direct creation cost and does not scale like mined text.
   - The essay says frontier robotics may need enormous data volumes, so the industry must price the marginal utility of each data dollar rather than celebrate volume.
2. The essay maps the main robot-data modalities.
   - Observational data is broad and relatively cheap, such as egocentric or exocentric video, but it lacks direct action supervision.
   - Interventional data is action-dense, such as teleoperation demonstrations, but it is expensive and scales with human labor.
   - Deployment data is generated by production systems, but its distribution is dictated by commercial operations rather than the model's need for novelty.
3. Scaling-law lessons make repetition and low variance look expensive.
   - More data helps by a power law with diminishing returns, while diversity can lower the error floor and expand the manifold a model covers.
   - Repetition has limited utility and can eventually hurt capability, especially when a narrow slice of data is over-sampled.
   - Rare out-of-distribution events carry high marginal utility because real-world performance is constrained by the long failure tail.
4. Deployment telemetry can become a convergence trap.
   - Production data behaves like an oil well: early anomalies may be valuable, but routine successes quickly become low-utility near-duplicates.
   - Commercially viable early deployments often require low-variance environments, which makes their data easier to collect but less useful for general foundation-model progress.
   - Garg argues that narrow deployment niches can lock companies into linear integration work unless broader observational and interventional inputs expand the capability boundary.
5. The recommended metrics replace volume with information density.
   - Teams should track marginal integration cost per novel task, task-level saturation points, distributional drift, cluster coverage, and data novelty density.
   - Interventional staging should stop at a task's saturation threshold, while deployment streams should filter for failures and out-of-distribution edge cases.
   - Garg's conclusion is that physical AI capital efficiency comes from accurately pricing data novelty, not maximizing cumulative operational hours.

### 5. Lean Software Scaling Laws

1. Gwern은 coding LLM scaling에 관한 research question에서 출발한다.
   - 이 제안은 source code에 대한 LLM perplexity가 context size 증가에 따라 어떻게 변하는지 측정해 codebase의 predictability를 추정할 수 있는지 묻는다.
   - 실천적 동기는 software safety다. 미래 coding LLM이 대부분의 software를 쓸 수 있지만, insecure하거나 quality가 낮은 generated code는 security를 악화시킬 수 있다.
   - Gwern은 더 나은 predictability exponent를 가진 language와 codebase가 결국 LLM이 이해하고, 고치고, 작성하기 쉬워질 것이라고 본다.
2. 이 글은 language prior와 장기 scaling behavior를 분리한다.
   - Python 같은 인기 language는 더 큰 training corpus 덕분에 현재 LLM이 기본적으로 잘 다루는 경우가 많다.
   - Gwern은 corpus size가 운명이 아니라고 주장한다. skill은 language 사이에서 부분적으로 transfer될 수 있고, 더 강한 model은 덜 흔한 language도 끌어올릴 수 있기 때문이다.
   - 핵심 질문은 짧은 script에 어떤 language가 쉬운지가 아니라, system이 수십만 또는 수백만 line에 도달했을 때 어떤 language가 계속 다루기 쉬운지다.
3. Lean은 high-upside지만 data가 부족한 후보로 제시된다.
   - Lean은 formal verification, 강한 constraint, memory-safety benefit, 중요한 correctness property를 prove할 가능성을 제공한다.
   - Bottleneck은 Lean source code가 많지 않아 LLM이 아직 큰 complex software를 Lean으로 autonomously translate할 만큼 강하지 않다는 점이다.
   - 이로 인해 chicken-and-egg 문제가 생긴다. large Lean codebase가 이미 있다면 유용한 Lean training data를 만들기 쉬워지기 때문이다.
4. Predictability가 제안된 measurement proxy가 된다.
   - poorly designed system은 reader와 model이 global state, override, undocumented behavior, runtime surprise, inconsistent patch를 추적하게 만든다.
   - well-architected system은 interface, type, invariant가 다음에 일어날 일을 constrain하기 때문에 system을 더 많이 볼수록 더 predictable해져야 한다.
   - Gwern은 perplexity 또는 bits per character를 system-level predictability에 대한 약하지만 측정 가능한 proxy로 쓰자고 제안한다.
5. Measurement plan은 crossover point와 failure mode를 찾는다.
   - 저비용 version은 frozen pretrained LLM, language별 source corpus, long context window의 loss measurement, position averaging, curve fitting, extrapolation을 사용한다.
   - 유용한 cross-check에는 subtle bug injection, artificial context limit 아래 compile-and-test rollout, type signature ablation, minimal-context experiment가 포함된다.
   - Gwern은 weak language가 small scale에서는 이길 수 있지만 scaling exponent에서는 질 수 있고, Lean은 absolute loss가 나쁘게 시작해도 exponent가 더 낫다면 결국 투자를 정당화할 수 있다고 예측한다.

### 6. Moneyball for Physical AI

1. Garg는 robot data를 capital-allocation problem으로 framing한다.
   - Moneyball analogy는 baseball team이 한때 눈에 보이지만 predictive power가 약한 metric에 돈을 썼고, 더 나은 team은 실제로 중요한 statistic을 분리했다는 것이다.
   - Physical AI에서 Garg는 raw operational hours가 misleading metric이라고 주장한다. robot data는 직접 creation cost가 있고 mined text처럼 scale되지 않기 때문이다.
   - 이 글은 frontier robotics가 enormous data volume을 필요로 할 수 있으므로, industry가 volume을 자랑하기보다 data dollar의 marginal utility를 pricing해야 한다고 말한다.
2. 이 글은 주요 robot-data modality를 mapping한다.
   - Observational data는 egocentric 또는 exocentric video처럼 broad하고 비교적 cheap하지만 direct action supervision이 없다.
   - Interventional data는 teleoperation demonstration처럼 action-dense하지만 expensive하고 human labor와 함께 scale된다.
   - Deployment data는 production system에서 생성되지만, distribution은 model의 novelty 필요가 아니라 commercial operation에 의해 결정된다.
3. Scaling-law lesson은 repetition과 low variance를 expensive하게 보이게 만든다.
   - More data는 diminishing return을 가진 power law로 도움을 주며, diversity는 error floor를 낮추고 model이 cover하는 manifold를 넓힐 수 있다.
   - Repetition은 utility가 제한적이고, narrow slice의 data가 over-sampled될 때 capability를 해칠 수 있다.
   - Rare out-of-distribution event는 real-world performance가 long failure tail에 의해 제한되기 때문에 높은 marginal utility를 가진다.
4. Deployment telemetry는 convergence trap이 될 수 있다.
   - Production data는 oil well처럼 작동한다. 초기 anomaly는 valuable할 수 있지만 routine success는 빠르게 low-utility near-duplicate가 된다.
   - Commercially viable early deployment는 대개 low-variance environment를 필요로 하며, 이는 data collection을 쉽게 만들지만 general foundation-model progress에는 덜 유용하다.
   - Garg는 broader observational input과 interventional input이 capability boundary를 넓히지 않으면 narrow deployment niche가 company를 linear integration work에 가둘 수 있다고 주장한다.
5. Recommended metrics는 volume을 information density로 대체한다.
   - Team은 novel task당 marginal integration cost, task-level saturation point, distributional drift, cluster coverage, data novelty density를 tracking해야 한다.
   - Interventional staging은 task의 saturation threshold에서 멈춰야 하며, deployment stream은 failure와 out-of-distribution edge case를 filtering해야 한다.
   - Garg의 결론은 physical AI의 capital efficiency가 cumulative operational hours maximization이 아니라 data novelty를 정확히 pricing하는 데서 나온다는 것이다.

5. Lean Software Scaling Laws

  1. Gwern starts with a research question about coding LLM scaling.
    • The proposal asks whether LLM perplexity over source code can estimate how predictable a codebase becomes as context size grows.
    • The practical motivation is software safety: future coding LLMs may write most software, but insecure or low-quality generated code could worsen security.
    • Gwern suggests that languages and codebases with better predictability exponents should eventually become easier for LLMs to understand, repair, and write.
  2. The essay separates language priors from long-run scaling behavior.
    • Popular languages such as Python benefit from larger training corpora, so current LLMs often perform well on them by default.
    • Gwern argues that corpus size is not destiny because skills can partially transfer across languages and stronger models may lift less common languages.
    • The key question is not only which language is easiest for a short script, but which language remains tractable as systems reach hundreds of thousands or millions of lines.
  3. Lean is presented as the high-upside but data-starved candidate.
    • Lean offers formal verification, strong constraints, memory-safety benefits, and the possibility of proving major correctness properties.
    • The bottleneck is that there is not much Lean source code, so LLMs are not yet strong enough to translate large complex software into Lean autonomously.
    • This creates a chicken-and-egg problem: useful Lean training data would be easier to create if large Lean codebases already existed.
  4. Predictability becomes the proposed measurement proxy.
    • A poorly designed system forces readers and models to chase global state, overrides, undocumented behavior, runtime surprises, and inconsistent patches.
    • A well-architected system should become more predictable as more of the system is seen, because interfaces, types, and invariants constrain what can happen next.
    • Gwern proposes using perplexity or bits per character as a weak but measurable proxy for that system-level predictability.
  5. The measurement plan looks for crossover points and failure modes.
    • The cheap version uses frozen pretrained LLMs, source corpora by language, loss measurement across long context windows, position averaging, curve fitting, and extrapolation.
    • Useful cross-checks include injected subtle bugs, compile-and-test rollouts under artificial context limits, ablations of type signatures, and minimal-context experiments.
    • Gwern predicts weak languages may win at small scale but lose on scaling exponents, while Lean may start with worse absolute loss yet eventually justify investment if the exponent is better.

6. Moneyball for Physical AI

  1. Garg frames robot data as a capital-allocation problem.
    • The Moneyball analogy is that baseball teams once paid for visible but weakly predictive metrics, while better teams isolated the statistic that actually mattered.
    • In physical AI, Garg argues that raw operational hours are the misleading metric because robot data has direct creation cost and does not scale like mined text.
    • The essay says frontier robotics may need enormous data volumes, so the industry must price the marginal utility of each data dollar rather than celebrate volume.
  2. The essay maps the main robot-data modalities.
    • Observational data is broad and relatively cheap, such as egocentric or exocentric video, but it lacks direct action supervision.
    • Interventional data is action-dense, such as teleoperation demonstrations, but it is expensive and scales with human labor.
    • Deployment data is generated by production systems, but its distribution is dictated by commercial operations rather than the model’s need for novelty.
  3. Scaling-law lessons make repetition and low variance look expensive.
    • More data helps by a power law with diminishing returns, while diversity can lower the error floor and expand the manifold a model covers.
    • Repetition has limited utility and can eventually hurt capability, especially when a narrow slice of data is over-sampled.
    • Rare out-of-distribution events carry high marginal utility because real-world performance is constrained by the long failure tail.
  4. Deployment telemetry can become a convergence trap.
    • Production data behaves like an oil well: early anomalies may be valuable, but routine successes quickly become low-utility near-duplicates.
    • Commercially viable early deployments often require low-variance environments, which makes their data easier to collect but less useful for general foundation-model progress.
    • Garg argues that narrow deployment niches can lock companies into linear integration work unless broader observational and interventional inputs expand the capability boundary.
  5. The recommended metrics replace volume with information density.
    • Teams should track marginal integration cost per novel task, task-level saturation points, distributional drift, cluster coverage, and data novelty density.
    • Interventional staging should stop at a task’s saturation threshold, while deployment streams should filter for failures and out-of-distribution edge cases.
    • Garg’s conclusion is that physical AI capital efficiency comes from accurately pricing data novelty, not maximizing cumulative operational hours.

    • 필요성은 이미 문서화를 하던 team과 아직 지식을 잘 정리하지 못한 team 모두에서 나왔다.
  3. 기존 documentation system에는 세 가지 핵심 문제가 있었다.
    • Static-site-generated docs는 repository clone, Markdown edit, pull request, review 대기 과정이 필요해 non-engineer에게 장벽이 높았다.
    • 기존 document tool에는 낡은 policy, 완성되지 않은 note, 맥락 없는 material이 쌓여 documentation debt가 됐다.
    • 지식은 SSG docs, document tool, code, internal messenger discussion, 개인의 기억 속에 흩어져 있었다.
  4. todoc은 knowledge usability을 중심으로 네 가지 product value를 세운다.
    • 출발점이 GitHub, 다른 document tool, internal messenger 어디든 누구나 쉽게 문서를 쓰고 고칠 수 있어야 한다.
    • todoc 안의 지식은 team bot, API, CLI, MCP를 통해 AI가 쉽게 활용할 수 있어야 한다.
    • Platform은 유효한 internal knowledge의 SSoT 역할을 하고, 각 team이나 계열사가 work를 문서화할 수 있는 확장 가능한 공간을 제공해야 한다.
  5. 남은 과제는 writing quality와 freshness를 system화하는 것이다.
    • Toss는 technical writer의 판단을 활용해 AI correction과 draft automation을 제공했지만, 글은 여전히 사람이 문서를 쓰기로 결심한다는 전제가 있다고 말한다.
    • 다음 목표는 decision, code change, discussion이 workflow 안에서 자연스럽게 document가 되게 만드는 것이다.
    • 장기 방향은 technical writer의 전문성을 stale knowledge 감지, improvement 제안, healthy governance 유지 system으로 바꾸는 것이다.

5. Lean Software Scaling Laws

  1. Gwern은 coding LLM scaling에 관한 research question에서 출발한다.
    • 이 제안은 source code에 대한 LLM perplexity가 context size 증가에 따라 어떻게 변하는지 측정해 codebase의 predictability를 추정할 수 있는지 묻는다.
    • 실천적 동기는 software safety다. 미래 coding LLM이 대부분의 software를 쓸 수 있지만, insecure하거나 quality가 낮은 generated code는 security를 악화시킬 수 있다.
    • Gwern은 더 나은 predictability exponent를 가진 language와 codebase가 결국 LLM이 이해하고, 고치고, 작성하기 쉬워질 것이라고 본다.
  2. 이 글은 language prior와 장기 scaling behavior를 분리한다.
    • Python 같은 인기 language는 더 큰 training corpus 덕분에 현재 LLM이 기본적으로 잘 다루는 경우가 많다.
    • Gwern은 corpus size가 운명이 아니라고 주장한다. skill은 language 사이에서 부분적으로 transfer될 수 있고, 더 강한 model은 덜 흔한 language도 끌어올릴 수 있기 때문이다.
    • 핵심 질문은 짧은 script에 어떤 language가 쉬운지가 아니라, system이 수십만 또는 수백만 line에 도달했을 때 어떤 language가 계속 다루기 쉬운지다.
  3. Lean은 high-upside지만 data가 부족한 후보로 제시된다.
    • Lean은 formal verification, 강한 constraint, memory-safety benefit, 중요한 correctness property를 prove할 가능성을 제공한다.
    • Bottleneck은 Lean source code가 많지 않아 LLM이 아직 큰 complex software를 Lean으로 autonomously translate할 만큼 강하지 않다는 점이다.
    • 이로 인해 chicken-and-egg 문제가 생긴다. large Lean codebase가 이미 있다면 유용한 Lean training data를 만들기 쉬워지기 때문이다.
  4. Predictability가 제안된 measurement proxy가 된다.
    • poorly designed system은 reader와 model이 global state, override, undocumented behavior, runtime surprise, inconsistent patch를 추적하게 만든다.
    • well-architected system은 interface, type, invariant가 다음에 일어날 일을 constrain하기 때문에 system을 더 많이 볼수록 더 predictable해져야 한다.
    • Gwern은 perplexity 또는 bits per character를 system-level predictability에 대한 약하지만 측정 가능한 proxy로 쓰자고 제안한다.
  5. Measurement plan은 crossover point와 failure mode를 찾는다.
    • 저비용 version은 frozen pretrained LLM, language별 source corpus, long context window의 loss measurement, position averaging, curve fitting, extrapolation을 사용한다.
    • 유용한 cross-check에는 subtle bug injection, artificial context limit 아래 compile-and-test rollout, type signature ablation, minimal-context experiment가 포함된다.
    • Gwern은 weak language가 small scale에서는 이길 수 있지만 scaling exponent에서는 질 수 있고, Lean은 absolute loss가 나쁘게 시작해도 exponent가 더 낫다면 결국 투자를 정당화할 수 있다고 예측한다.

6. Moneyball for Physical AI

  1. Garg는 robot data를 capital-allocation problem으로 framing한다.
    • Moneyball analogy는 baseball team이 한때 눈에 보이지만 predictive power가 약한 metric에 돈을 썼고, 더 나은 team은 실제로 중요한 statistic을 분리했다는 것이다.
    • Physical AI에서 Garg는 raw operational hours가 misleading metric이라고 주장한다. robot data는 직접 creation cost가 있고 mined text처럼 scale되지 않기 때문이다.
    • 이 글은 frontier robotics가 enormous data volume을 필요로 할 수 있으므로, industry가 volume을 자랑하기보다 data dollar의 marginal utility를 pricing해야 한다고 말한다.
  2. 이 글은 주요 robot-data modality를 mapping한다.
    • Observational data는 egocentric 또는 exocentric video처럼 broad하고 비교적 cheap하지만 direct action supervision이 없다.
    • Interventional data는 teleoperation demonstration처럼 action-dense하지만 expensive하고 human labor와 함께 scale된다.
    • Deployment data는 production system에서 생성되지만, distribution은 model의 novelty 필요가 아니라 commercial operation에 의해 결정된다.
  3. Scaling-law lesson은 repetition과 low variance를 expensive하게 보이게 만든다.
    • More data는 diminishing return을 가진 power law로 도움을 주며, diversity는 error floor를 낮추고 model이 cover하는 manifold를 넓힐 수 있다.
    • Repetition은 utility가 제한적이고, narrow slice의 data가 over-sampled될 때 capability를 해칠 수 있다.
    • Rare out-of-distribution event는 real-world performance가 long failure tail에 의해 제한되기 때문에 높은 marginal utility를 가진다.
  4. Deployment telemetry는 convergence trap이 될 수 있다.
    • Production data는 oil well처럼 작동한다. 초기 anomaly는 valuable할 수 있지만 routine success는 빠르게 low-utility near-duplicate가 된다.
    • Commercially viable early deployment는 대개 low-variance environment를 필요로 하며, 이는 data collection을 쉽게 만들지만 general foundation-model progress에는 덜 유용하다.
    • Garg는 broader observational input과 interventional input이 capability boundary를 넓히지 않으면 narrow deployment niche가 company를 linear integration work에 가둘 수 있다고 주장한다.
  5. Recommended metrics는 volume을 information density로 대체한다.
    • Team은 novel task당 marginal integration cost, task-level saturation point, distributional drift, cluster coverage, data novelty density를 tracking해야 한다.
    • Interventional staging은 task의 saturation threshold에서 멈춰야 하며, deployment stream은 failure와 out-of-distribution edge case를 filtering해야 한다.
    • Garg의 결론은 physical AI의 capital efficiency가 cumulative operational hours maximization이 아니라 data novelty를 정확히 pricing하는 데서 나온다는 것이다.
